question: Does a neighbourhood base explain Lightroom Highlights better than the pixel luminance?

method.input: Lightroom pairs neutral -> Highlights variant, pixel-aligned
method.predictor: x = (1 - alpha) log2 Y + alpha log2 base; base Gaussian (sigma) or guided filter (radius, eps in EV^2) of log2 Y, in analysis pixels
method.explanatory: per scene RMS of e = log2(Y1/Y0) around its median per 0.25 EV bin of x
method.predictive: leave-one-scene-out mean of per-scene bin medians; y * 2^(g L(x)), clipped at 1
method.criterion: mean sRGB-encoded Y of the 10 % brightest neutral pixels, prediction / LR - 1
method.gains: none, or ideal per scene (upper bound)

limits: Simulated on the LR neutral: isolates the operator, not IPR's development
Luminance only; colour handling (darkenKeepingColour) not modelled
Ideal gain is an upper bound, not a predictor
Analysis at 1/8 resolution: detail finer than 8 px is not assessed
